we present an algorithm for embedding a 4-connected planar graph G with n ≥ 4 vertices on a grid of width W and height H, with W + H ≤ n, W ≤ ( n + 3 ) /2 and H ≤2( n - 1 ) /3, in linear time.

the following question: What is the minimum area required to draw an n-vertex planar graph in a straight line grid?

the problem of finding a grid embedding of minimum area for a given plane graph.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the embedding of 4- connected graphs on a straight-line grid is a problem which is still not fully solved, and the results obtained so far are not sufficient to solve it completely.
a 4-connected planar graph G with at least four vertices in the external face can be embedded on an (n - 1) × n grid in linear time.
the problem of determining whether a graph has a straight-line embedding on a given grid is NP-complete.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the grid embedding of plane graphs is NP-hard for general graphs, and can be solved in linear time for 4-connected graphs.
we have given an algorithm that embeds 4-connected graphs in a grid of size at most W × H, where W + H = n and W ≤ (n - 3)/2.
the straight line grid embeddings of 4-connected plane graphs are characterized by two parameters W and H.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a grid embedding of a 4-connected graph G with at least four vertices in its outer face is not much larger than a grid embedding of G with no vertices in the outer face.
the number of grid points in the external face is a good predictor of the grid size of the embedding.
we can embed a 4-connected planar graph on a grid with O(n) area.
